evals.name: auto-full-release
evals.prompt: /ship
evals.expected_output: Runs the whole release in auto mode without asking: minor bump from feat commits, version updated in every source including package-lock.json, sweep with no missed hit, reviewer PASS, tag pushed and confirmed, GitHub release created, npm publish for an already-published package, and a final report that lists each auto decision.
expectations: Asks the user no confirmation question at any step.
Prints Mode: auto in the Step 1 report and in the final report.
Chooses a minor bump because the commits since the last tag include feat: and no breaking change, and states that rule.
Updates both version fields in package-lock.json (top-level version and packages[""].version), not only package.json.
Runs the old-version git grep sweep after applying changes and reports 0 missed hits with the counts of other classes.
Spawns the release-reviewer before writing any project file and continues only on PASS.
Confirms the pushed tag with git ls-remote before creating the GitHub release.
Publishes to npm only after checking that the package already exists on npm and the new version does not.
The final report's first line is Result: COMPLETE, PARTIAL — <reason>, or BLOCKED — <reason>.
Evidence names the check behind each claim; anything not verified, such as a clean install, appears under Uncertainty.
Decision names a pending user action or states No approval needed.

evals.name: interactive-mode
evals.prompt: /ship --no-auto
evals.expected_output: Runs the same release but stops for confirmation before the version, the consolidated file changes, the build, the push, the GitHub release, and the publish.
expectations: Prints Mode: interactive in the Step 1 report.
Asks the user to confirm or override the computed version before spawning subagents.
Shows the consolidated summary under four headings (version, changelog, docs, landing page) and waits for confirmation before writing files.
Asks before running the build, before pushing, before creating the GitHub release, and before publishing.
If the user declines the push, ends with Result: PARTIAL — tag vX.Y.Z created locally, not pushed.

evals.name: auto-dirty-tree-blocks
evals.prompt: /ship (the working tree has a modified src/app.ts and an untracked notes.txt)
evals.expected_output: Stops in Step 1 with Result: BLOCKED — uncommitted changes, lists both files, and changes nothing: no stash, commit, discard, version bump, or tag.
expectations: Stops before Step 2 and reports Result: BLOCKED — uncommitted changes.
Lists src/app.ts and notes.txt under Evidence.
Does not stash, commit, restore, or delete any file.
Decision tells the user to commit or stash the changes and re-run, or to use /ship --no-auto.

evals.name: notes-only-scope
evals.prompt: What changed since the last release? Draft the release notes for me.
evals.expected_output: Runs pre-flight, the version analysis, and the changelog-generator only, shows the developer changelog and the plain-language end-user notes, and changes no project files: no commit, tag, push, GitHub release, or publish.
expectations: Does not modify, commit, tag, push, or publish anything.
Shows a developer changelog grouped by category with PR links.
Shows end-user notes grouped under New, Improved, Fixed, or Action needed, with no commit hashes, PR numbers, or author handles.
States that this was a notes-only request, so no release steps ran.

evals.name: landing-page-four-items
evals.prompt: /ship (the repo has site/index.html with a v1.4.2 version pill, a footer that still says v1.4.0, a What's new section, a features grid, and an install section; the release adds a PDF export feature)
evals.expected_output: The landing-page-updater reports version, end-user changelog, feature list, and documentation, each with a status and path:line; it fixes both the pill and the stale footer version, rewrites What's new in plain language, adds a PDF export feature card, and adds no new section.
expectations: Reports all four landing-page items (version, changelog, features, docs), each as updated, current, or not on page with path:line evidence.
Updates the stale v1.4.0 footer as well as the v1.4.2 pill.
Rewrites the What's new section from user-notes.md without commit hashes, PR numbers, author handles, or conventional-commit prefixes.
Adds a feature card for PDF export that matches the existing card markup.
Does not add a section the page did not already have.
The landing-page-updater, not the version-bumper, owns the version lines in site/index.html, so each line is changed once.

evals.name: unreleased-and-drift
evals.prompt: /ship (CHANGELOG.md has a ## Unreleased section with three entries; package.json says 2.3.0 but src/version.ts still says 2.2.9)
evals.expected_output: Promotes the Unreleased section to the release heading and adds a fresh empty Unreleased heading, so the release appears once; reports src/version.ts as a drifted version source and updates it to the new version.
expectations: Retitles the existing ## Unreleased section as the release heading instead of adding a second entry with the same changes.
Leaves an empty ## Unreleased heading above the new release entry.
Lists src/version.ts as a drifted version source (2.2.9) and updates it to the new version.
After applying, every version source reads the new version.

evals.name: zero-major-breaking
evals.prompt: /ship (the last tag is v0.9.3 and one commit since then is feat!: drop the legacy config format)
evals.expected_output: Releases v0.10.0, not v1.0.0, because auto mode never crosses to 1.0.0 without an explicit version argument; records the rule under Evidence and the breaking change as an Action needed item in the end-user notes.
expectations: Chooses 0.10.0, not 1.0.0, and states the 0.y.z breaking-change rule.
Writes the breaking change as an Action needed step in user-notes.md.
Adds upgrade instructions for the dropped config format to the changelog entry.

evals.name: negative-open-pr
evals.prompt: Open a pull request for my feature branch so the team can review it.
evals.expected_output: Does not run ship; opening a PR is not a release.
expectations: Does not start the ship workflow.
Does not bump a version, create a tag, or publish anything.

evals.name: negative-routine-commit
evals.prompt: Commit my changes with a good message and push them.
evals.expected_output: Does not run ship; a routine commit and push is not a release.
expectations: Does not start the ship workflow.
Does not create a tag or a GitHub release.

evals.name: feature-branch-blocks
evals.prompt: ship it (current branch is feat/export, which has an open PR; the default branch is main)
evals.expected_output: Stops in Step 1 with Result: BLOCKED — not on the default branch, before any version bump, commit, tag, release, or publish, and says a release from another branch needs --no-auto.
expectations: Compares the current branch with the default branch from refs/remotes/origin/HEAD or git remote show origin.
Reports Result: BLOCKED — not on the default branch.
Does not bump a version, commit, tag, push, create a GitHub release, or publish.
Decision says to merge the PR first, or to re-run with --no-auto to release from feat/export.

evals.name: breaking-footer-major
evals.prompt: /ship (the last tag is v2.3.0; one commit since then is 'feat: new config loader' whose body has the footer 'BREAKING CHANGE: config.yml is renamed to app.yml')
evals.expected_output: Detects the BREAKING CHANGE footer in the commit body and releases v3.0.0, with an Action needed item in the end-user notes and upgrade steps in the changelog.
expectations: Reads commit bodies, not only subjects, and finds the BREAKING CHANGE footer.
Chooses 3.0.0, not 2.4.0, and states the rule.
user-notes.md tells users to rename config.yml to app.yml under Action needed.

evals.name: release-tool-auto
evals.prompt: /ship (package.json has "scripts": {"release": "release-it"})
evals.expected_output: Detects release-it and stops with Result: BLOCKED — release owned by release-it, without running npm run release, and gives the command under Decision.
expectations: Does not run npm run release or release-it.
Reports Result: BLOCKED — release owned by release-it.
Decision gives the project's release command (npm run release) or suggests /ship --no-auto.

evals.name: tagged-head-different-version
evals.prompt: /ship 1.2.4 (clean default branch; HEAD and the package version are v1.2.3 / 1.2.3; v1.2.3 is fully released, with no later commits; 1.2.4 has no tag or registry publication)
evals.expected_output: Treats 1.2.4 as a new release: syncs, selects the explicit version, prepares and reviews the changes, builds, and releases 1.2.4. Does not resume or report 1.2.3 as the requested release.
expectations: Does not enter the resume path just because HEAD has the v1.2.3 tag.
Runs normal repo sync and Step 2 version selection, choosing 1.2.4 from the explicit argument despite the empty since-tag log.
Runs the normal preparation, review, sweep, and build for 1.2.4 before tagging or publishing it.
Does not recreate or republish 1.2.3.

evals.name: tagged-head-explicit-bump
evals.prompt: /ship patch (clean default branch; HEAD has the fully released v1.2.3 tag, package.json says 1.2.3, and there are no later commits; v1.2.4 is unused)
evals.expected_output: Follows normal sync and version selection, computes 1.2.4 from the explicit patch argument, and prepares a new release rather than resuming 1.2.3.
expectations: An explicit bump argument does not enter the tagged-HEAD resume path.
Chooses 1.2.4 by applying patch to 1.2.3 and does not stop with nothing to release.
Prepares and reviews the new release instead of skipping Steps 2-5.
Reports the explicit patch argument as the version-selection rule.

evals.name: tagged-head-same-version-resume
evals.prompt: /ship 1.2.3 (clean default branch; HEAD has v1.2.3, which is already pushed and has a GitHub release; npm already has this project's 1.2.3; no local build artifacts exist)
evals.expected_output: Resumes the requested 1.2.3 release, verifies its existing tag, GitHub release, and npm publication, and reports them done without bumping, rebuilding, or uploading again.
expectations: Accepts the exact matching explicit version as a resume, rather than blocking on the existing tag or registry version.
Skips sync and version preparation and reuses the existing commit and tag.
Verifies npm's existing 1.2.3 publication and performs no local build, npm publish, retag, or release recreation.
Reports the verified steps as done before the stop and names 1.2.3 as the release.

evals.name: resume-npm-fresh-clone-build
evals.prompt: /ship (fresh clone on a clean default branch at tagged HEAD v1.2.3; tag and GitHub release are already on origin; package.json has main=dist/index.js, files=[dist], and a build script that creates dist/index.js; dist/ is ignored and absent; npm belongs to this repository but has only 1.2.2; credentials work and no CI publishes)
evals.expected_output: Resumes 1.2.3, runs the required build to regenerate dist/index.js, verifies it is included in npm pack --dry-run, and only then publishes and verifies npm 1.2.3.
expectations: Does not assume the earlier release build's ignored artifacts exist in the fresh clone.
Runs the required npm build before the unfinished local npm upload.
Confirms dist/index.js exists and is in the npm pack --dry-run file list before npm publish; packing only package.json does not pass.
Reuses the existing version, commit, tag, and GitHub release without preparing or tagging a new release.
Reports the build, package validation, and registry verification under Evidence.

evals.name: resume-npm-build-failure
evals.prompt: /ship (fresh clone on a clean default branch at tagged HEAD v1.2.3; tag and GitHub release are already pushed; npm 1.2.3 is still unpublished and the local upload is authorized; package.json requires dist/index.js, dist/ is absent, and npm run build fails)
evals.expected_output: Runs the required resume build, stops with Result: BLOCKED — build failed, and performs no package upload. Reports the failed build and the unfinished npm publication while preserving the existing release.
expectations: Runs npm run build before attempting a local upload.
Stops with Result: BLOCKED — build failed when that command fails.
Does not run npm publish or accept npm pack success as a substitute for the failed build.
Does not delete or recreate the existing release commit, tag, or GitHub release.
Evidence records the failed build and Decision identifies the remaining build repair and npm publication.

evals.name: poetry-only-pypi-metadata
evals.prompt: /ship 1.2.4 (clean default branch; pyproject.toml has [tool.poetry] name=existing-project and version=1.2.3, no [project] table, and [build-system] uses poetry-core; PyPI's existing-project belongs to this repository and has only 1.2.3; credentials work, no CI publishes, and 1.2.4 has no tag)
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the Poetry package as a PyPI publishing target, checks ownership and target-version availability before edits, updates [tool.poetry] version, builds and validates the distribution, and publishes 1.2.4.
expectations: Recognizes [tool.poetry] name with [build-system] as a PyPI package even without [project] or setup.py.
Checks the existing package's repository ownership and that PyPI 1.2.4 is absent before changing files.
Updates [tool.poetry] version to 1.2.4 and builds the distribution using the configured build backend.
Runs distribution validation before uploading and verifies the published PyPI version.
Does not skip PyPI solely because the package metadata uses [tool.poetry].

evals.name: ci-publisher-existing-target-blocks
evals.prompt: /ship 1.2.4 (clean default branch with commits after v1.2.3; v1.2.4 does not exist locally or on origin; npm package belongs to this repository and already has 1.2.4; a tag-triggered GitHub workflow runs npm publish)
evals.expected_output: Selects CI as the publisher but still checks npm's target version before edits, then stops with Result: BLOCKED — 1.2.4 already on npm without creating or pushing a release tag.
expectations: Treats CI ownership as publisher selection and continues through private, repository-ownership, and target-version checks.
Queries npm for 1.2.4 before preparing or applying release changes.
Reports Result: BLOCKED — 1.2.4 already on npm despite the unused release tag.
Does not change files, commit, tag, push, or trigger the publishing workflow.
Does not defer the duplicate-version failure until CI publishing.

evals.name: ci-publisher-no-local-credentials
evals.prompt: /ship 1.2.4 (clean default branch with commits after v1.2.3; npm package belongs to this repository, is public, and has only 1.2.3; 1.2.4 has no tag or registry publication; a tag-triggered GitHub workflow has publishing credentials and succeeds, but this machine is not logged into npm)
evals.expected_output: Checks registry eligibility and target-version availability, selects the CI publisher, and runs the release without requiring local npm credentials. After pushing the tag, verifies the workflow and npm 1.2.4 instead of uploading locally.
expectations: Runs private, repository-ownership, and target-version checks before any release file changes despite CI ownership.
Does not require npm whoami or local upload credentials for the CI publisher.
Does not skip publication or report PARTIAL solely because this machine is not logged into npm.
After the tag push, waits for the matching CI workflow and verifies npm 1.2.4.
Does not run a duplicate local npm publish.

evals.name: first-ci-publication-needs-registry-request
evals.prompt: /ship (clean default branch with commits after v1.2.3; package.json names a public npm package that has never been published; a tag-triggered GitHub workflow has credentials and runs npm publish; the request does not name npm)
evals.expected_output: Rejects the first npm publication without an explicit registry request and stops with Result: BLOCKED — CI publication not authorized before any release edits or publishing trigger event.
expectations: Checks first-publication eligibility even though the publisher is CI.
Reports Result: BLOCKED — CI publication not authorized because the package is unpublished and the request does not name npm.
Does not prepare or apply release file changes, commit, tag, push, or create a GitHub release.
Does not treat a skipped local upload as sufficient to prevent the CI publication.
Evidence names the first-publication gate and Decision identifies the missing explicit registry request.

evals.name: first-ci-publication-explicit-registry
evals.prompt: Publish this release to npm with /ship 1.2.4 (clean default branch with commits after v1.2.3; package.json names a public package not on npm; a tag-triggered GitHub workflow has credentials and runs npm publish; 1.2.4 has no tag and this machine is not logged into npm)
evals.expected_output: Accepts the explicit npm request for the first publication, checks the remaining registry and release gates, then releases 1.2.4 and verifies its CI publication without requiring local npm credentials or uploading twice.
expectations: Records that the explicit npm request permits the first registry publication.
Continues registry eligibility and target-version checks before release file changes.
Does not require local npm login for the CI publisher.
After the tag push, verifies the matching workflow and npm 1.2.4 publication.
Does not run a duplicate local npm publish.

evals.name: unprefixed-breaking-footer-priority
evals.prompt: /ship (clean default branch; last tag and package version are v2.3.0 / 2.3.0; the only new commit has subject 'Remove old config' and footer 'BREAKING CHANGE: config.yml is renamed to app.yml'; there are no conventional-commit subject prefixes)
evals.expected_output: Detects the breaking footer and chooses 3.0.0 before considering the no-prefix minor fallback. The release reviewer validates the breaking bump, and the notes explain the config migration.
expectations: Reads the commit body and detects its BREAKING CHANGE footer despite the unprefixed subject.
Chooses 3.0.0, not 2.4.0, and records the breaking-change rule.
Does not apply the no-conventional-prefix fallback when a breaking subject or footer was detected.
The release reviewer checks breaking-change bump consistency even for a no-prefix fallback proposal and rejects a minor bump when metadata reports this breaking change.
The end-user notes and documentation explain the config.yml to app.yml migration.

evals.name: nonbreaking-no-prefix-fallback
evals.prompt: /ship (clean default branch; last tag and package version are v2.3.0 / 2.3.0; the only new commit has subject 'Improve config diagnostics' and a body with no breaking-change marker; there are no conventional-commit prefixes)
evals.expected_output: Preserves the no-prefix fallback: chooses 2.4.0 and reports 'no conventional commits, defaulted to minor' under Uncertainty, while the release reviewer checks the proposed bump against the nonbreaking metadata.
expectations: Checks subjects and bodies for breaking changes before selecting the no-prefix fallback.
Chooses 2.4.0 because there are no conventional prefixes and no breaking change.
Records 'no conventional commits, defaulted to minor' under Uncertainty.
Does not infer a breaking change or choose a major bump solely from an unprefixed subject.
The release reviewer includes this fallback in its version-consistency check.
